## Experiment

`coop --git` with 250 steps and compaction at 64K, the same per-agent budget as the best `solo` run (250 steps, 64K). Tests whether `coop` and `solo` differ when each agent gets the same budget.

| Model | `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash`, high thinking |
| Subset | `flash_10` (10 pairs) |
| Step limit | 250 per agent |
| Compaction | at 64K tokens |
| Passed | 8/10 (80%) |
| Agents stopped at the step limit | 1 |
| Merge conflicts | 0 |

| Cost | `$21.68` (`$2.17` per pair) |

## Observations

- 8/10, the same 8 pairs as both `coop` runs with 28K compaction. Compared with `solo` at the same budget (7/10), the only difference is `dspy_task/8394`, which is within run-to-run chance.
- With more room before summarizing, agents compacted much less (median 3 times per agent) and 19 of 20 submitted before step 250.
- `pallets_jinja_task/1559`: one agent submitted a 242-line patch for its feature, the first real submission on this pair in any run. Its partner was stuck for 70 minutes on a test command that never finished (we stopped it by hand), then hit step 250 with a 1-line patch that did not apply. When one patch does not apply, the grader tests only the first agent's patch against both features, so the pair failed.
- `pillow_task/290`: both agents submitted and the patches merged cleanly, but feature 4 failed 1 of its 8 tests, the same as `coop` without the shared remote.
- The 70-minute stuck command made the run's wall time longer (242 minutes), not its result different.
